title: Coast Guard members rescue 2 people, 1 cat from sinking houseboat
description: Coast Guard members from Elizabeth City, N.C., rescue two people and their cat after their houseboat began to sink on the Scuppernong River near the Albemarle Sound, June 13, 2020. In this video, the members describe their response to the case. U.S. Coast Guard video.
keywords: Cat, Air Station, sinking, ELIZABETH CITY, Albemarle, Taking on Water, Houseboat, kealy, Andrada, Coast Guard, rescue, USCG, small boat

transcript.text: (upbeat music)
- And check this out.
The kind of news we need today.
Coast Guard members from Elizabeth City
came to the rescue this morning.
- [Narrator] The Coast Guard rescuing a couple and their cat
from a sinking houseboat off the Carolina coast
- [Reporter] The couple called 911 when their houseboat

along the Scuppernong River near Elizabeth city.
- We got the call for a 50 foot houseboat
taking on water with two people and a cat on board.
And as soon as the alarm goes off
the whole crew is rushing to the helicopter.
A good Samaritan called on the radio
and said that they had found the houseboat
that the coast guard was looking for.
So thanks to them,
we were able to find them much more quickly.
We sent the rescue swimmer down, and he swam to the boat,

because we weren't confident in the stability of the vessel.
We were a little concerned about hoisting the cat

So thankfully the small boat arrived on scene
and they were able to get the cat.
- On 30th of June, we received a report,
a 50 foot vessel with two people and a cat on board.

the rescue team was hoisting the second survivor
when they got word that the cat was still on board.
- [Michael] So alongside the vessel,
I remember McCann and I got the okay to go in the water
by Petty Officer Reese
We then entered through the window into chest high water.
I then retrieved the cat and handed it to fireman McCann,
who then handed it to Petty Officer Cloin on the small boat.
Something that I'll remember

with its owner, and the joyful expression on her face.
(laughing)
- Thank you so much.
- You're welcome.
- And after we were on deck before they had gotten off,

And that's really when it hit home
